classification.difficultyReason: Explore dimensions with a fixed area, compare their perimeters and identify the minimum without restricting dimensions to whole numbers.

content.prompt: Investigate the possible perimeters for a rectangle of area $64\text{ m}^2$. Which of the alternatives has the smallest perimeter?

answer.short:
An $8\text{ m}\times8\text{ m}$ square has the smallest perimeter, $32\text{ m}$.

Compare rectangles whose length multiplied by width is $64$.
answer.worked:
Choose dimensions whose product is $64$. Some possibilities are:
$$\begin{align*}
P_{1\times64}&=2(1+64)=130\text{ m}\\
P_{2\times32}&=2(2+32)=68\text{ m}\\
P_{4\times16}&=2(4+16)=40\text{ m}\\
P_{6.4\times10}&=2(6.4+10)=32.8\text{ m}\\
P_{8\times8}&=2(8+8)=32\text{ m}
\end{align*}$$
There are infinitely many possibilities because the side lengths need not be whole numbers. For a fixed area, the smallest perimeter occurs when the length and width are equal. Here, $8\times8=64$, so the square has the smallest perimeter, $32\text{ m}$.
